name: Adaptive Local Models (ALM)
analogy: Think of it as a trader who, instead of trusting one rulebook, flips back through a diary and pulls out only the days that looked like today. They draw a quick best-fit line through just those days, weighting the closest lookalikes most, and make a forecast from it.

steps.title: Keep every observed transition
steps.description: The model does not compress history into fixed weights. It stores each past step as a record of the state, the action taken and what happened on the next bar.
steps.inExample: The store holds 12,000 past steps from 5-minute Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures bars, each with its features, position and next-bar change.

steps.title: Describe today's situation
steps.description: When a prediction is needed, the current state and the action being considered are written in the same form as the stored records.
steps.inExample: The query is the 14:10 bar with an oversold reading, with the candidate action being to buy one contract.

steps.title: Find the closest past situations
steps.description: Every stored record is given a distance from the query. A weight is then assigned that is large for near lookalikes and fades quickly to almost nothing for distant records.
steps.inExample: The 60 nearest records get meaningful weight; the other 11,940 are close to zero.

steps.title: Fit a small model to just those neighbours
steps.description: A simple weighted best-fit line is solved from the weighted records only. It is thrown away after the prediction, so each query gets a model made to measure for its own neighbourhood.
steps.inExample: A weighted line is fitted through the 60 neighbours, relating the features and the action to the next-bar change in points.

steps.title: Predict the next bar and its uncertainty
steps.description: The fitted line is evaluated at the query to give the expected next-bar change. The spread of the neighbours around the line gives a rough measure of how much to trust it.
steps.inExample: The model predicts a rise of about 2 points for a buy, with typical neighbour scatter of 9 points.

steps.title: Add the new outcome to the store
steps.description: After the next bar arrives, the real outcome becomes another stored record. The model adapts by simply having more, and more recent, neighbours to draw from.
steps.inExample: The 14:15 result is appended, making the store 12,001 records long.

useFor.task: A one-step forecast inside a planning loop
useFor.example: Supplying the next-bar prediction that a controller re-solves every bar to choose between holding, buying and selling.

useFor.task: Volatility forecasts that depend on the situation
useFor.example: Forecasting the next bar's range using only past bars with a similar opening gap and volume ratio.

useFor.task: Estimating slippage from similar past fills
useFor.example: Predicting the cost of a market order from earlier orders of similar size at similar times of day.

useFor.task: Adapting after a break in market behaviour
useFor.example: Letting predictions shift toward post-break records as they accumulate, without retraining anything.

avoidWhen: Predictions must be extremely fast on millions of stored records, because each query searches the whole store; a trained gradient boosting model answers in a fraction of the time.
The state has many dimensions, since lookalike days become scarce and distances lose meaning; a model that learns a compact representation is the better choice.

example.scenario: A planning loop on 5-minute Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures (MNQ) bars needs a one-step forecast of the next bar's change for the action of buying one contract at 14:10.

input.summary: The query state and action, and the store the neighbours are drawn from.

fields.name: stored transitions
fields.meaning: The number of past steps kept in memory, each with its next-bar outcome.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the 14:10 five-minute bar closed.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading; the market is leaning oversold.

fields.name: candidate action
fields.meaning: The action whose consequence the model is asked to predict.

fields.name: neighbours used
fields.meaning: How many nearest past records receive meaningful weight.

output.summary: A predicted next-bar change for the action, and how much to trust it.

fields.name: predicted next-bar change
fields.meaning: The expected move over the next five-minute bar if the contract is bought, about 4 US dollars.

fields.name: neighbour scatter
fields.meaning: Typical distance of the neighbours' real outcomes from the fitted line, a rough measure of uncertainty.

fields.name: effective neighbours
fields.meaning: The count of neighbours after weighting, which shows how thin the local evidence is.

fields.name: distance to nearest neighbour
fields.meaning: How close the most similar past record is compared with the usual gap between stored records; a large value means today is unlike anything stored.

example.reading: A forecast of 2 points against a scatter of 9 is a small lean buried in noise, so treat it as one input to the planner rather than a trade signal. If the distance to the nearest neighbour is large, distrust the forecast and let the planner fall back to a cautious default.
